about.heading: Who I am
paragraphs: First-year Bachelor's student in Computer Science at EPSI Paris. What draws me to computer science is understanding the entire stack — not just plugging into a framework.

On the code side, I work with PHP, JavaScript and SQL. On the infrastructure side, I build networks on VirtualBox and use Linux daily. On the hands-on side, I built a chain-reaction machine that won a contest, and an IoT platform tracking soil moisture.
I learn by building. When something breaks, I want to know why.

hero.title: About
hero.bio: First-year Bachelor's student in Computer Science at EPSI Paris. What I love: understanding systems, breaking things to fix them, and shipping projects that work.

blocks.title: My background
blocks.body:
I earned my mathematics baccalauréat with high honors (16.28/20) in July 2025 at Lycée Amara Rachid in Algiers. In parallel, I had already started coding: an intensive web development bootcamp at Code213 (Algiers), 192 hours of HTML, CSS and JavaScript basics. That's when I knew this was what I wanted to do.

I joined EPSI Paris in 2025 for my Bachelor's in Computer Science. Today, I'm doing a Full Stack internship at Glikt in Courbevoie.

blocks.title: Why computer science
blocks.body:
What draws me isn't just writing code. It's understanding how everything holds together. From the TCP packet traveling, to the SQL query responding, to the CSS aligning a button — everything is connected. I love that full-stack dimension.

At EPSI, I didn't want to specialize too early. I'm aiming for excellence across three axes: web, networking, embedded. I'll dive deeper later. For now, I'm building on all three.

blocks.title: How I work
blocks.body:
I learn by building. Theory in the morning, code in the afternoon. When something breaks, I don't work around it — I want to know why. That's usually where I learn the most.

In teams, I like concrete roles. On the Rube Goldberg project, I was in charge of the Tinkercad design. We won the contest.
